resources.string: This phone doesn\'t let apps act as caller ID, so the popup can\'t work on it.
Copies your phone model and setup status, without any phone numbers, so you can send it to whoever helps you.
Unknown numbers get a popup to look them up in Telegram.
When you tap Look up, the number is sent to this bot on Telegram. The bot is run by a third party.
Popup not allowed: tap Fix under Setup
Lets Android pass the app the number of unknown callers. Your contacts are never shared with the app.
Choose %1$s when Android asks which caller ID app to use.

If no prompt appears:
1. Open Settings → Apps → Default apps
2. Tap Caller ID & spam app
3. Choose %1$s
Turn on Allow display over other apps, then come back.
Tap Allow when Android asks whether %1$s may always run in the background.
If a settings page opens instead:
Switch the list to All apps, tap %1$s and choose Don\'t optimize. Then come back.
Choose Unrestricted, then come back. If App info opens instead, tap Battery first.
Turn on Allow background usage, then tap it and choose Unrestricted. If App info opens instead, tap App battery usage first.

Can't find it? Use this path instead:
1. Open Settings → Apps → Special app access
2. Tap Battery optimization
3. Switch the list to All apps
4. Tap %1$s and choose Don't optimize
Can\'t find it? Open Settings → Apps → %1$s → App battery usage, and choose Unrestricted under Allow background usage.
Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO phones don\'t let apps start in the background unless Autostart is on.
Find %1$s in the list and turn on Autostart, then come back.
If a different screen opens:\n1. Open Settings → Apps → Manage apps → %1$s\n2. Turn on Autostart
Did you turn on Autostart for %1$s?
Xiaomi has its own pop-up permissions. Without them the popup never appears, even when everything else is allowed.
Allow \"Display pop-up windows while running in the background\" and \"Show on Lock screen\", then come back.

If a different screen opens:
1. Open Settings → Apps → Manage apps → %1$s
2. Tap Other permissions
3. Allow both options above
Did you allow both pop-up options for %1$s?
OPPO, realme and OnePlus phones stop apps that aren\'t opened often, which can stop the popup.
Turn on Auto launch for %1$s, then come back.

If a different screen opens:
1. Open Settings → Apps → %1$s
2. Tap Battery usage
3. Turn on Allow background activity and Allow auto launch
Did you allow %1$s to run in the background?
vivo and iQOO phones block apps from starting and showing pop-ups in the background.
Turn on Autostart and background pop-ups for %1$s, then come back.
If a different screen opens:\n1. Open Settings → Apps → %1$s → Permissions\n2. Allow Autostart and Display pop-up windows in the background
Did you allow background pop-ups for %1$s?
Huawei and Honor phones close apps they manage automatically, which can stop the popup.
Find %1$s, turn off Manage automatically, then turn on Auto-launch, Secondary launch and Run in background.
If a different screen opens:\n1. Open Settings → Battery → App launch\n2. Find %1$s and set it as above
Did you set %1$s to launch manually?
Tap to install the new version.
So you hear when a new version of the app is out. Nothing else is sent as a notification.
So the popup closes by itself when the call ends.
So the caller\'s number appears on top of the call screen.
So Android doesn\'t put the app to sleep and miss calls.
So Android doesn\'t remove these permissions if you don\'t open the app for a few months.
Numbers are looked up through a Telegram bot.
Find %1$s in the list and turn it on, then come back.
Turn off \"Pause app activity if unused\", then come back.
Install Telegram from the store, then come back.

Android may block this as a "Restricted setting". To allow it:
1. Open Settings → Apps → %1$s
2. Tap ⋮ in the top corner
3. Tap Allow restricted settings
4. Come back and try again
Unknown callers will now get a popup to look them up in Telegram.
